data.description:
## Description

**What**: Extend tests/scripts/test-create-dso-app-real-url.sh (opt-in via RUN_REAL_URL_E2E=1; runs daily in CI) with failing integration tests for the new flow. Cover: Rails default end-to-end (working app + USWDS + SDK gem in Gemfile + DSO overlay files + tickets orphan branch + post-build SDK functional check); --template=nextjs scaffold without SDK gem; --template=flask scaffold without SDK gem; --no-sdk skip; --no-overlay skip; --port=8080 propagates to upstream app_local_port; --auto-install-prereqs unattended; A2-idempotency assertion (zero diffs on dso-config.conf, ARCH_ENFORCEMENT.md, project-understanding.md Strata Posture section against A2's onboarding-time idempotency check).

This is the **integration RED test story** for an external-API epic. Tests must fail before any implementation story (S1-S8, S10) lands.
**Why**: Real-URL behavioral test is the contract that the rewrite preserves user-visible scaffolding behavior; it gates the fork archive.
**Scope**:
- IN: New test cases extending the existing file; opt-in env var preserved; CI daily schedule preserved; A2-idempotency cross-check assertion.
- OUT: Implementing the installer phases (other stories).

## Done Definitions
- When complete, integration tests for Rails + nextjs + flask + flag variants are written and run under RUN_REAL_URL_E2E=1 ← Satisfies: SC1, SC2
- When complete, tests are confirmed FAILING (RED) before any implementation story begins. Failing run result recorded as a ticket comment: `.claude/scripts/dso ticket comment <this-story-id> "RED confirmed: <test output summary>"` ← Satisfies: SC1
- When complete, A2-idempotency cross-check assertion is in place ← Satisfies: SC1
- When complete, unit tests written and passing for any new harness helpers introduced

## Considerations
- [Testing] Tests must be run and confirmed failing (RED) before any implementation story begins
- [Reliability] Daily CI scheduling preserved
- [Testing] SDK functional check runs inside Docker; gate on Docker availability

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
